messages.subject: real/integer data in ODE
parts:
Dear all,
I'm trying to use ODE solver to fit a TKTD model (similar to PKPD) but I've some difficulties to give input parameters.

The model is as follow (see attached file for more details):

dx/dt = ke * (C(t) - x(t))
dy/dt = kk * max(0,x(t) - z) + m

C(t) is a,n observation made at specific time.

So, in stan, I wrote it like this :

dydt[1] = ke * (x_r[t] - y[1]);
     
max_z1[1] = 0;
max_z1[2] = y[1] - z;

dydt[2] = kk * max(max_z1) + hb;


The previous code dose not work. How x_r is suppose to change with time ?

Also, How I could vectorized it ? When I try, I always have "fourth argument to integrate_ode_rk45 must have type real[] for requested solution times; found type=real[,]"

Thank you

to be data.

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: real/integer data in ODE
parts:
I had a look at your model. Is this what you're trying to do with x_r : https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/58 ?

I think as of now there's not a clean built-in way to interpolate data like that in an ODE in Stan.

I think the issue is you need a smooth interpolation -- a simple 1D linear interpolation isn't differentiable at the data points. I think a lot of us with ODEs have run into this.

There's a dude in that post who shows a solution. I dunno how well it works. At one point I had a pretty simple function to interpolate and was able to approximate it using a cosine/sine expansion with a few terms (FFT).

Not sure on the vectorization. I think an ODE solve is usually a slow enough thing that there isn't a reason to try to vectorize it.

Ben

Well, after several hours on it, I do not understand how to interpolate something in an ODE function.

Considering observation `x_r` at time `ts_1, ts_2, ...`, and with integration done on time `t`, how could I wrote the interpolation?

Here is an example of the idea:


real[] TKTD( real t, // time
             real[] y, // variable
             real[] prm, // parameters
             real[] x_r, // real data
             int[] x_i) { // integer data

...
// And here is supposed to be the linear interpolation (sorry for wrong notation, of course 'i' is unknown):
real x_interpol;
x_interpol = x_r(ts[i]) + (t + ts[i]) * (x_r(ts[i+1]) - x_r(ts[i]))/(ts[i+1] - ts[i]);

// to add this in the ODE:
dydt[1] = ke * (x_interpol - y[1]);

return dydt

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: real/integer data in ODE
parts:
Yeah, linear interpolation is the thing you can't do very easily.

What you're saying in your comments is that you need to cast your time value (a real) to an integer somehow so you can index a lookup table somewhere.

I don't think there's a way in Stan to do this cast (correct me if I'm wrong?) because casting real parameters to integers messes up the derivatives you need for sampling. I think I misspoke about the linear interpolation differentiability thing (separate issue kinda).

That's why I ended up using a basis expansion for my function (cause then you never need to do this cast).

If you can build:

f_approx(t) = sum over i (a_i * basis_i(t))

Then there's no need to cast t from a real to an int.

You could do this with any sorta regression tool you want. Whatever is appropriate for the data. You may be able to build this regression into Stan, but dunno how much you want to try to do with one inference.

Not sure if this is a good way to proceed though. I didn't succeed with my inference, but I think it was more my problem. Maybe someone else knows a way to do this? I don't want to mislead you.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: real/integer data in ODE
parts:
You can interpolate without messing up derivatives if you're
careful, but to do it in Stan's a real hack because we don't
have a function to round/floor/ceiling a real value to an int.

If someone can characterize a general form of interpolation,
we could also build it in the way BUGS does.

- Bob
